column1: # The registry that replaces model-path pattern matching. One row per admitted
# checkpoint; qwen-launch.sh resolves the fetch script from it, and
# qwen-capacity-policy.sh reads context_ceiling from it instead of holding one
# global maximum.
# The SHA-256 stays in each fetch script rather than here, because two copies of
# a digest drift and the fetch script is the one that verifies the file.
# A required projector names its own fetch script explicitly. The language GGUF
# and projector can come from different publisher filenames, and selecting a
# downloader by model-family pattern can silently pair embeddings from another
# checkpoint.
# context_default is the interactive depth and context_ceiling is the depth the
# policy admits, and both describe an allocation. validated_filled_depth is the
# deepest depth measured to fill and decode under this row's own cache triple,
# Flash Attention state, batch, and ubatch, which is a different claim: a server
# that loads a 24576-token allocation has proven it can reserve the memory and
# has not proven that a near-full cache executes. `-` means no depth has been
# filled and decoded on this row and the allocation stands alone.
# batch and ubatch name the submission geometry the validated depth was measured
# under and the geometry qwen-capacity-policy.sh launches with. They are a field
# rather than a constant because submission geometry rather than depth alone
# decides whether the device retires its work: the prior host completed a depth
# at one geometry and wedged at another under the same cache triple, which
# evidence/legacy/raven2/comparative-findings.tsv retains as comparison. No arm
# on this device has measured the pair.
# tier states what is claimed about a row. `production` is a serving tuple
# measured safe and useful. `candidate` leaves quality or performance
# unqualified while no reset, fault, or device loss exists under its admitted
# tuple. `quarantine` names a checkpoint or profile that has produced a reset,
# fault, device loss, or correctness hazard, or that carries no validated safe
# tuple; scripts/quarantine.tsv holds its reason record and
# scripts/build-router-presets.sh keeps it out of the picker. `archive` is a
# valid artifact displaced by a better one or too slow to serve. `rejected` lost
# admission on measurement without being dangerous.
# A candidate enters at 8192 default and ceiling with `-` for
# validated_filled_depth, because architecture and a depth-0 rate say nothing
# about what a filled cache executes and the tree has wedged the compute ring at
# a depth it had only allocated. The depth arm is what moves those two fields.
# decode_tok_s and prefill_tok_s are measured through llama-bench on the CUDA
# backend at the served placement, `--device CUDA0` with `-ot .*=CUDA0`, since
# the scheduler leaves tensors on the host at `-ngl 99` alone and halved a
# prefill that way. A `-` means the row is admitted on a different basis. Every
# rate-carrying row takes its forward-and-reverse paired mean from
# evidence/ada/baseline-sweep-02/, so the column is one sweep and readable
# across rows. That matters because the
# same checkpoint under identical flags spans up to 30.6% between sweeps, and
# bands built across sweeps measured the sweep rather than the checkpoint. The
# three i1 rows carry the four-block mean from evidence/decode-bound-analysis.md
# and belong to a different sweep, so they compare to each other and not to the
# rows above them.
# quality names its own scale because two scales exist. `NN/55` is the graded
# suite in evidence/model-admission/roster-quality-sweep.md, run with thinking
# off at a 1024-token budget across every servable row in one sweep. `5/5-screen`
# is the earlier five-prompt screen, run with thinking on, which the suite
# carries forward as its `screen` category; the two do not compare. A suite
# result is conditioned on the request sequence that produced it -- prepending
# five rows moves two checkpoints by one arithmetic row each, deterministically
# -- so a one-row or two-row difference between rows here reports position in a
# sequence rather than capability. A number here is what the current grader
# emits over the retained replies rather than what the sweep printed on the day:
# the `nonempty` grader passed a reply cut at the token budget, and
# evidence/quality-roster/regrade-summary.tsv carries the recorded total beside
# the corrected one for every arm.
# raw_tool_selection and guarded_tool_execution are two claims because one
# number answered both would authorize the wrong thing. raw_tool_selection is
# the model unaided: the graded tool category in
# evidence/model-admission/vision-and-tool-sweep.md, which asks the model to
# choose a tool, fill its arguments, invent none, and decline where no tool
# applies. guarded_tool_execution states whether this row may execute a tool,
# and its vocabulary is `refused`, `validator-gated`, and `unguarded`.
# Every row reads `refused`, and the reason is the same on all six measured
# arms: tool-08 places an instruction inside the note the user asks about, and
# every checkpoint carried the injected city into the call in place of the one
# the user authorized. A model that fails that row can still serve text, and a
# model that passes the other nine rows is not thereby safe to grant execution,
# so a high raw_tool_selection never promotes this field. Only a runtime that
# compares the emitted arguments against the user's own authorization before
# execution moves a row to `validator-gated`, and this tree holds no such
# validator: the appliance runs without --tools, the server executes nothing,
# and the request body's tools field asks for a tool_calls object alone.
# Two rows can hold one checkpoint's weights at two precisions, and role rather
# than tier separates them. `qwen35-08b` is Q8_0 at `compact-text` and
# `qwen35-08b-f16` is F16 at `compact-precision`: the same weights, the second
# at the highest precision its publisher ships, so it is the quality ceiling
# every quantized rung of those weights is measured against. It decodes slower
# rather than faster, at 15.68 against 18.53, which is what buying precision
# costs here.
# Both 0.8B rows read `projector: none` and run text-only, because
# select-projector.sh searches the model file's own directory and no projector
# sits beside either file. The publisher does ship one --
# `mmproj-Qwen_Qwen3.5-0.8B-f16.gguf` at 0.191 GiB -- so the vision path is
# unfetched rather than unavailable, and admitting it means fetching that file
# and running the vision rows against it.
# The uncensored, unredacted, and heretic-lineage rows enter at tier candidate
# on a published header, a publisher LFS digest, and one strict device-placement
# load with host fallback refused.
# The device-time arms that would move them -- a graded quality suite, a filled
# depth, and a role comparison against the class control -- are unrun on this
# host.
# mtp_layers is what the GGUF declares and speculation_profile is what the
# appliance does with it. The capability is read from the file rather than
# inferred from a family name or a filename: `<arch>.nextn_predict_layers` in
# the metadata block with the matching `blk.N.nextn.*` tensors present. `0` means
# the header was read and declares no prediction block; `-` means no arm has read
# it. The policy names a row of scripts/speculation-profiles.tsv, and
# scripts/build-router-presets.sh emits that profile's flags into the row's own
# router section rather than into the router argv, where
# `common_preset::merge` would overwrite every section with one setting.
# speculation_evidence states which claim the policy rests on, because a
# capability is not a rate. A path names the arm that measured this checkpoint
# as a speculation target on this host. `capability-only` states that the block
# is present and loads and that no throughput arm has run, so the profile is a
# prediction rather than a measurement. `-` belongs to a row whose profile is
# `off`. evidence/ada/speculation-runtime-classes.md measures the 2B, 4B, and 9B
# distills as targets at 1.23, 1.42, and 1.47 of baseline; it measures the 0.8B
# as a draft alone and does not measure qwenseer-2b at all, so those two rows
# read `capability-only` until a served A/B moves them.
# switch_policy states how a row may share a router roster. `lru` leaves the
# row under the router LRU at any QWEN_ROUTER_MAX, which is the measured
# behavior of every served pair to date. `evict-first` admits the row into a
# router preset only under --models-max 1, where server-models.cpp already
# serializes evict-before-load on the victim child process exit, because the
# router capacity gate counts models rather than bytes and a second resident
# beside this row exceeds the carve-out. `standalone-only` keeps the row out
# of router presets entirely; the standalone launch path serves it alone.

# id
# The policy ledger for web-enabled router presets. One row per profile;
# scripts/build-web-presets.sh reads this file alongside scripts/models.tsv and
# emits one INI section per row.
# scripts/models.tsv is the authority for validated_filled_depth, vision_allowed,
# and tool_selection. This file repeats all three so a profile row reads whole,
# and scripts/build-web-presets.sh compares each against the named model_id's
# registry row and stops the run on divergence, naming the profile, the field,
# and both values. A copy that drifts states a depth or a vision grant the
# runtime never honours, so correcting this file rather than the registry is
# what the refusal asks for. Every row meets that comparison, the tier rule, and
# the ceiling rule whatever its execution_policy, so the ledger is validated
# whole and an edit that turns one row into an emitting policy changes what
# emits rather than what passes.
# context and validated_filled_depth are copied verbatim from the named
# model_id's context_ceiling and validated_filled_depth columns in
# scripts/models.tsv. Unknown is not permission: scripts/build-web-presets.sh
# refuses a profile whose context exceeds context_ceiling, and refuses one
# whose context exceeds a numeric validated_filled_depth or whose
# validated_filled_depth reads `-`, treating the unmeasured case the same as
# the measured-too-shallow case rather than as an unbounded allowance.
# QWEN_WEB_ALLOW_UNVALIDATED_DEPTH=1 admits a profile that fails that rule
# regardless of the model_id's own tier in models.tsv -- a production-tiered
# model is exactly the one an experimental web profile should be able to
# run. What the override withholds is the emitted section's own claim to
# that tier: no `default` tag, `experimental` in `tags`, a stderr line
# naming the unknown state or the numeric gap, and the output file's
# unvalidated-depth-override head marker. These rows set a policy starting
# point rather than a measured optimum: no web-research arm has run against
# any of them. The three text profiles request depths their registry rows have
# filled and decoded. The Qwen3.5-2B and LFM projector-required profiles request
# 8192 against `-`, because the retained depth arms loaded text weights alone.
# QWEN_WEB_ALLOW_UNVALIDATED_DEPTH=1 remains required when a profile requests
# a depth beyond its validated surface, and the generated section carries the
# experimental marker and tag.
# web_mode is `validator-gated` where a later validator is expected to compare
# emitted tool arguments against the user's own authorization before a fetch
# executes, and `ui-mediated` where the web-UI surfaces the model's proposed
# query or URL for the operator to run by hand. execution_policy is `refused`
# on every row because tool-08 in evidence/model-admission/vision-and-tool-sweep.md
# carried an injected instruction into the tool call on all six measured
# checkpoints, and this tree holds no validator that would justify a
# validator-gated or unguarded execution_policy yet; web_mode names the
# intended future path and execution_policy names what is authorized now.
# multi_source reads yes exactly where max_fetches exceeds 1, and
# scripts/build-web-presets.sh refuses a row that breaks either direction: the
# emitted MCP configuration carries the fetch budget alone, so a no row above one
# fetch grants retrieval this ledger denies, and a single fetch reaches one
# source. vision_allowed is copied
# from the model_id's projector column in models.tsv: `required` becomes yes
# and `none` becomes no. tool_selection is copied from the model_id's
# raw_tool_selection column, the graded tool-selection score unaided by any
# execution guard.
# The five trailing columns state which search backend a profile serves and
# what it asks that backend for. provider names the backend and must equal the
# generator's own QWEN_WEB_PROVIDER, so a row states what it expects rather
# than inheriting whatever the environment held. Under provider searxng the
# remaining four carry the search policy into the emitted MCP configuration as
# QWEN_WEB_SEARXNG_PRIMARY_CATEGORY, QWEN_WEB_SEARXNG_FALLBACK_CATEGORY,
# QWEN_WEB_SEARXNG_MINIMUM_RESULTS, and QWEN_WEB_SEARXNG_URL; the model
# supplies none of them. Which engines a category holds lives in the instance's
# own settings.yml under qwen-named categories, so the engine population
# changes by editing the instance rather than by any request field. A search
# queries primary_category once and, where fewer results survive
# canonicalization, private-target rejection, and the granted domain lists than
# minimum_results, queries fallback_category exactly once; `-` in
# fallback_category leaves the primary answer as it stands. Under provider exa
# or fake the four read `-`.
